tasks.title: Sum of two numbers
tasks.prompt: What is the sum of 23 and 47?

tasks.title: Total cost
tasks.prompt: A store sells apples at $0.50 each and bananas at $0.30 each. If you buy 10 apples and 15 bananas, what is the total cost?

tasks.title: Average speed
tasks.prompt: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the average speed in miles per hour?

tasks.title: Profit after tax
tasks.prompt: A company had revenue of $200,000 and expenses of $120,000. The tax rate is 20% on profit. What is the net profit after tax?

tasks.title: Compound interest
tasks.prompt: You invest $1000 at an annual interest rate of 5% compounded yearly. What is the amount after 2 years?

tasks.title: Pump filling tank with conversion and leak
tasks.prompt: A tank holds 480 gallons and already contains 60 gallons. A pump delivers 7.57 litres per minute. Use 1 gallon = 3.785 litres exactly as stated. While filling, a leak drains 0.5 gallons per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the tank completely? Answer with a single number only: the number of minutes (no units, no formula).

tasks.title: Probability with replacement, exact decimal
tasks.prompt: A bag contains 3 red counters and 5 blue counters (8 in total). A counter is drawn at random, replaced, and a second counter is then drawn at random from the full bag. What is the probability that exactly one of the two draws is red? Answer with a single number only: the probability as a decimal (for example 0.46875), with no percent sign.

tasks.title: Crew schedule with inclusive dates and weekends
tasks.prompt: A road crew works on every day from 4 May 2026 through 15 May 2026, inclusive of both the first and last day. On weekdays (Monday to Friday) the crew works 7 hours per day. On Saturdays the crew works 4 hours per day. On Sundays the crew does not work. How many total working hours does the crew work in this period? Answer with a single number only: the total number of hours (no units).

tasks.title: Compound percentage changes
tasks.prompt: An investment starts at 24,000 dollars. In year 1 it increases by 18 percent. In year 2 it then decreases by 12.5 percent. In year 3 it then increases by 10 percent. Each percentage change applies to the value at the start of that year. What is the final value in dollars? Answer with a single number only: the final value in dollars (no dollar sign, no commas).
